gen-fs-panchang-archivo: Panchang pushes out wide, confident strokes that never pinch at a curve. Archivo sits taller in the lowercase and more editorial, so the two feel like a loud voice and a friendly one trading lines.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-fira-sans: Panchang's strokes hold steady like a drawn string, with open space between every stem and curve. Fira Sans follows with a larger lowercase and no thick-and-thin swing, giving the display face a sturdy partner.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-gambetta: Panchang glows with a thickness like neon glass tubing, bold and expressive across the top of the page. Gambetta's gently shifting strokes stay comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-panchang-montserrat: Panchang's strokes run with the steadiness of a drawn string, never snagging on a closed-up bowl. And Montserrat glides beneath it with generous white space leading into each curve, so the heading feels confident and the body feels welcoming.
gen-fs-panchang-outfit: Outfit reads clean and approachable, its curves finishing well before they close. Its strokes are bent like cable, so the sans stays better for brief copy while Panchang carries the bolder, display-sized voice above it.
gen-fs-panchang-sora: Panchang keeps wide stretches of blank between each stem and curve, confident and expressive. Its job is display flair, while Sora, precise and geometric, is good for a handful of lines.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-asap: Paquito's lowercase fills the line like capitals, sturdy and warm. And Asap, with open arcs on its c and a body height nearly matching its capitals, carries a longer passage along smoothly beside it.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-public-sans: Sturdy, warm, and nearly all capital-height in its lowercase, Paquito makes a firm opening. But Public Sans answers with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, so the serif heading and the sans-serif body both feel dependable.
gen-fs-paquito-montserrat: Montserrat reads geometric and approachable, with white space leading into each curve and a line that glides like wire. And its monoline strokes set against Paquito's sturdy serif give the pair a clear, memorable contrast.
gen-fs-pencerio-fs-chillax: Graceful and formal, Pencerio writes in a calligraphic hand with closely fitted word shapes. Chillax loosens everything up beneath it, its same-width strokes trailing like spaghetti and made for short stretches of reading.
